title: Reservation Slicing and Canary Autoscale for Dedicated Tenants
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Introduce a deterministic "reservation slicing" model and a staged (canary) autoscale pathway for Dedicated tenants to improve utilization while protecting reserved SLAs. Reservation slicing enables a tenant's reserved allocation to be segmented into smaller timed slices that can be borrowed by low-risk workloads; canary autoscale provides a safe, incremental path for transient burst capacity that respects isolation and rollback policies.
background: Customers with reserved Dedicated capacity want lower unit cost while retaining isolation guarantees. Current rigid reserved pool semantics cause unused capacity to sit idle, leading to waste and higher customer TCO. Past approaches (full backfill, unbounded soft-burst) caused noisy neighbor incidents and SLA violations. We need a middle-ground that increases effective utilization without compromising predictable reserved performance.
goals: (1) Increase effective utilization of reserved capacity by enabling safe short-term borrowing of idle slices. (2) Provide an automated, observable, and reversible canary autoscale flow for bursts that maintains tail-latency SLOs for reserved tenants. (3) Surface controls in the Console so tenants can configure conservative to aggressive borrowing profiles.
non_goals: This PRD does not cover: billing changes for cross-tenant backfill (billing will remain per-commit for this phase), deep changes to the kernel scheduling runtime beyond conservative knobs exposed, or the full multi-region failover/autoscale mix (will be handled in a follow-up).
user_stories: As a platform engineer, I want each reserved contract to be splittable into slices so low-priority background tasks can use unused slices without impacting SLA-critical requests.
As an SRE I want canary autoscale to provision a small fraction of burst capacity first and monitor latency before expanding, so we can safely admit more load.
As a tenant admin I want Console controls to select a borrowing aggressiveness profile (Strict / Balanced / Opportunistic) and view historical slice usage, so I can trade cost vs isolation.
As oncall I want automatic rollback and preemption thresholds tied to percent tail latency and error rate, so incidents are self-protecting.
As a product manager I want telemetry that attributes borrowed-slice usage to tenant, time window, and triggering workload so we can measure impact on utilization and incidents.
requirements: Reservation slicing: ability to declare a reservation as N time-slices (default 24 slices of 1 hour) with configurable slice granularity per tenant.
Borrow semantics: idle slices can be leased to other low-priority tenants/workloads with a maximum lease time and immediate reclaim capability.
Isolation guardrails: a reclaim pathway that preempts borrowed slices when reserved tenant latency or error thresholds exceed configured limits.
Canary autoscale flow: when burst demand occurs, provision an initial canary allocation (e.g., 5% of requested burst) and evaluate latency/error for T minutes before expanding in defined steps.
Rollback triggers: define clear SLO-tripping thresholds (e.g., p99 latency > baseline + 2x or error rate increase > 1.5x) that cause immediate shrink to safe capacity and alerting.
Console controls and defaults: three aggressiveness presets (Strict, Balanced, Opportunistic) plus advanced mode exposing slice count, lease TTL, canary step sizes, and triggers.
API: expose reservation-slicing and canary-autoscale options on Dedicated capacity API and SDKs (create/update reservation endpoints).
Telemetry: emit metrics and logs for slice allocation, lease events, preemptions, canary steps, rollback reasons, and tenant-visible decisions for auditability.
Backward compatibility: existing reservations without slicing remain unchanged unless tenant opts in; default profile for legacy reservations is Strict (no borrowing).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Feature flags gate both reservation slicing and canary autoscale; disabled by default.

2) On a staging cluster, demonstrate 20-40% increase in transient consumable capacity using Balanced profile without exceeding reserved tenants' p99 latency SLO (measured across 30-day synthetic workload test).
3) Console UI: Aggressiveness presets visible and editable in reservation edit flow; historical slice utilization chart present in reservation detail page.
4) API: new fields accepted by the reservations API; validation errors for invalid combinations; documented in SDK changelog.
5) Reclaim path: borrowed slices are preempted within 30s of a reserved-tenant SLO trigger and incoming reserved requests resume with <= 5% cold-start overhead compared to baseline.
6) Canary autoscale: canary step evaluates telemetry for configured observation window and either expands or rolls back; automated rollback tested in chaos scenarios.
7) Security: feature passes security review for multi-tenant isolation and does not expose tenant identifiers in logs beyond existing principles.
8) Monitoring/Alerting: new alerts created for rollback events, preemptions exceeding threshold, and unhandled borrow lease expirations; alert noise validated on staging.
9) Documentation: PRD, Console screenshots, API docs, and runbook for rollbacks/oncall accessible in the linked Confluence page.
success_metrics: Increase effective reserved utilization by at least 15% for tenants who opt into Balanced or Opportunistic within 60 days of launch.
Zero customer-facing SLA incidents attributable to borrowed-slice preemptions in first 90 days for tenants on Strict or Balanced profiles.
Time-to-reclaim median <= 15s and 95th percentile <= 30s during test-induced pressure.
Reduction in idle-reserved-capacity metric (unused reserved GPU-minutes) by 20% for participating tenants.
ui_changes: Reservation detail page: new panel 'Slicing & Burst' with current slice map, historical usage heatmap, and preset toggles.
Reservation create/update flow: radio for aggressiveness presets + 'advanced' link that opens modal with slice count, TTL, canary step size, and rollback thresholds.
Alerts/Events feed: new event types for 'slice leased', 'slice reclaimed', 'canary expanded', and 'canary rolled back' with link to reservation.
RBAC: only tenant admins and org owners can change aggressiveness beyond default.
api_contract: PATCH /v1/dedicated/reservations/:id accepts fields: slice_count (int), slice_ttl_seconds (int), borrowing_profile (enum), canary_step_percent (int), canary_window_seconds (int), rollback_triggers (list of strings).
GET /v1/dedicated/reservations/:id returns current slice map and active leases with lease expiry timestamps (no raw tenant secrets).
Events emitted to existing events stream with event_type and reservation_id and reason.
telemetry: Metrics: reserved.slice_leased_count, reserved.slice_reclaimed_count, reserved.canary_step_count, reserved.rollback_count, reserved.reclaim_latency_seconds (histogram).
Logs: structured lease grant/revoke records with anonymized decision_reason code (e.g., 'spike', 'manual', 'slo_violation').
Tracing: trace points for canary provision -> observe -> expand/rollback for correlating latency regressions.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (feature flags + small internal dogfood): enable for internal teams only; validate reclaim latency and rollback behavior (2 weeks).
Phase 1 (beta customers): invite 5 low-risk tenants to opt into Balanced profile; monitor for 4 weeks and iterate on thresholds.
Phase 2 (wider opt-in): open opt-in to all self-serve tenants with Guardrails; collect telemetry for 30 days.
Phase 3 (on-by-default for Opportunistic is NOT planned): Evaluate automatic recommendations in Console (read-only) after 90 days of stable metrics.
Rollback plan: feature flag off for specific reservations or global; automatic rollback if rollback_count spike > threshold.
migration_strategy: No forced migration. Existing reservations remain Strict by default. Tenants must opt-in via Console or API to enable slicing.
Provide a one-click UI helper to safely convert a reservation to a sliced reservation with recommended defaults based on historical utilization.
dependencies: Serving runtime: reclaim API hook that can preempt KV cache and active batches (ENG scheduling and runtime teams).
Console: UI components and events plumbing, Console team implementation and design assets.
Billing: for future phases if cross-tenant billing for borrowed slices is required (not in scope).
Security review and audit logging changes (Security & Compliance team).
risks: Noisy neighbor incidents if reclaim is slow or canary thresholds are too permissive.
Increased operational complexity leading to alert fatigue for oncall if default thresholds are poorly tuned.
Telemetry volume increases; cost of metrics and retention may rise.
Tenant confusion if Console UX exposes advanced knobs without clear defaults and recommendations.
open_questions: Should slice granularity default to 1 hour or be workload-derived (e.g., 5–30 minute slices for bursty workloads)?
Exact preemption SLA: is 30s acceptable for all reserved SLAs or do some tenants require stricter reclaim windows?
Should borrowing be limited to tenants within the same organizational trust boundary for compliance-sensitive customers?
How will we report borrowed-slice usage on invoices if customers want a clear cost split in future phases?
notes: We should run chaos experiments that artificially hold slices to simulate slow reclaim behavior before wide rollout.
Consider a 'trial credit' in Console for tenants who opt-in so they can evaluate cost impact without committing to longer contracts.
Coordinate with Customer Success to find beta tenants that are comfortable with staged rollouts.
